name: West African
notes: West African (Guinean/Malian djembe tradition) — FOUNDATION RELEASE, deliberately incomplete. This pack ships what can be honestly taught from public knowledge without a lineage teacher: rhythm-name literacy, drum-break ear training, the canonical class ritual, grounded posture, and generic preparatory movement. The movement repertoire per rhythm — the actual dances — is CONSULTANT-PENDING by design (see meta.lineage_honesty and docs/AFRICAN-PARTNERSHIPS.md): these dances live in lineages (the Koumbassa/Camara school of teaching descends from Les Ballets Africains), and authoring their steps without a tradition-bearer would be exactly the extraction Doc 02 §3 warns against. The drum is the teacher here: every dance belongs to a rhythm, and the BREAK (the djembe call) cues every transition.

teachers.name: Cumbe Center (Brooklyn) — Guinean/West African classes incl. Mouminatou Camara
Youssouf Koumbassa — master teacher, workshops & Guinea immersions

seasons.finale: Film yourself naming three rhythms blind (dundunba, kuku, lamban) from recordings — and catching every break.
Film 2 minutes in grounded posture moving with a djembe track — bent, alive, never rigid.
Film your across-the-floor: the class-format travel step, 4 passes, arriving with the break.
Take a live West African class with drummers. This tradition is taught in rooms with drums — go.
In class, take your turn in the circle. One phrase is enough. That's the tradition welcoming you.

attributes.name: Break ear L1
attributes.test: hear the djembe break (the call) and stop/start on it, 10 for 10, across three different recordings

attributes.name: Grounded posture L1
attributes.test: 2 minutes moving in bent-knee, flat-back-forward posture without locking upright — the earth-focused stance

attributes.name: Line stamina L1
attributes.test: 6 across-the-floor passes at class tempo, form intact

nodes.name: One rhythm, one dance: how the tradition organizes itself
checkpoints: every dance belongs to a rhythm, an occasion, a meaning — kuku is not 'a beat', it is an event
the djembe and dunun ensemble is the teacher; dancers answer it

nodes.name: The break (the call): the drum's sentence that starts and stops everything
checkpoints: the break is the djembe phrase that cues entrances, changes and endings
train it like a language: listen daily until your body flinches on it

nodes.name: Dundunba — the dance of the strong (Malinké, Guinea)
checkpoints: a family of rhythms from Hamana (Kouroussa), historically the strong men's circle dance
learn its dunun melody until you can hum it

nodes.name: Kuku — the celebration circle (forest Guinea)
checkpoints: celebration rhythm of the forest region, danced in a circle; among the first taught worldwide
feel how it swings differently from dundunba — that difference IS the literacy

nodes.name: Lamban — the griots' rhythm (Mande)
checkpoints: the rhythm of the jeliw (griots) — praise, history, celebration
three rhythms named blind is the season's test: dundunba, kuku, lamban

nodes.name: Name three rhythms blind + catch every break
Lineage: Les Ballets Africains to the diaspora classrooms
checkpoints: these dances travel through teachers, not videos — Youssouf Koumbassa and Mouminatou Camara carry the Guinean stage tradition worldwide
having permission from a teacher in the tradition matters here; it is how the lineage continues

nodes.name: The class ritual: warm-up → breakdown → lines to the drummers → circle
checkpoints: the format is nearly identical worldwide — learn it before you walk in
dancing TOWARD the drummers in lines is the heart of class; the closing circle is the community

nodes.name: Grounded posture (the earth-focused stance)
checkpoints: knees bent, weight into the earth, back long and pitched from the hips
flat feet that CARESS the ground — this tradition dances INTO the floor, not off it
arms live wide and alive, moving from the back
this stance is preparation, not choreography — the dances themselves come from a teacher

nodes.name: Échauffement (the warm-up run)
checkpoints: light driving run in place, arms pumping from the back
it ends ON the break — that's the whole game: move until the drum says stop

nodes.name: Across-the-floor travel step (generic class preparation)
checkpoints: step-together-step with grounded knees, arms swinging open
travel toward imaginary drummers; arrive with the break
a PREPARATION for class lines — the true steps per rhythm come from your teacher

nodes.name: The honest limit: the dances come from tradition-bearers
checkpoints: this pack deliberately does NOT teach the dance repertoire per rhythm — that content belongs with lineage teachers, in partnership, credited and paid
what it CAN honestly give you: rhythm literacy, break ears, grounded posture, class readiness — you'll walk into class prepared instead of lost
the partnership plan for the full pack is public: docs/AFRICAN-PARTNERSHIPS.md

nodes.name: The scene bridge: a live class with drummers
checkpoints: find a class with LIVE drumming — the dialogue between drum and dancer is the tradition
arrive knowing the ritual, the rhythms' names and the break; the teacher gives you the rest

nodes.name: Taking your turn in the circle
